title: stage-prober: adaptive prefetch fusion for low-latency prefill-decode overlap
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduce Stage Prober component that enables adaptive, latency-first prefetch fusion of prefill and decode stages. Improves tail latency for mixed short/long prompts by overlapping chunked prefill with speculative decode while preserving token-level KV cache correctness.
description: Motivation: production traces show two dominant latency modes when serving short+long mixed workloads: (1) wasted idle time while waiting for full prefill to complete before decoding, and (2) decode stalls caused by late KV priming when speculative decode runs ahead. This PR introduces a Stage Prober and an adaptive prefetch fusion strategy that dynamically decides per-request chunking and speculative decode windows to maximize stage overlap without violating KV cache consistency guarantees. Key changes: 1) New runtime component 'stage_prober' that samples live request sequences and exposes a per-model, per-batch hint API to the scheduler; 2) Adaptive prefetch fusion algorithm that computes a safe speculative decode horizon based on prefix entropy, sequence-length histogram, and current KV warmness score; 3) Chunked prefill executor that can prefill in micro-chunks with KV write coalescing to reduce blocking; 4) Kernel hint metadata plumbing: kernels receive an aggressive|balanced|conservative hint to tune attention caching and contiguous memory copies; 5) Soft-evict TTL for KV entries to reduce thrash when speculative prefetch aggressively primes entries that are unlikely to be used; 6) Continuous batching adjustments to favor fast-turnaround cohorts when prober signals low-latency mode; 7) extensive microbenchmarks and regression tests with synthetic and production-sampled workloads. Performance summary: internal canary on p4d with a mixed workload (60% short prompts <= 16 tokens, 40% long streams) shows median latency reduction of 18%, 95th percentile down 26%, and token throughput improvement of 7% under steady load. Tail behavior when prober is disabled is unchanged. Backwards compatibility: all existing model configs are supported; default behavior is conservative until customers opt into the per-model prober hints via the Console or model config. Rollout plan: staged feature flag rollout in three phases (internal canary -> selected customers on dedicated -> general rollout), with a fallback that disables speculative horizon and reverts to full prefill. Checklist: [x] unit tests for chunked prefill executor [x] e2e canary harness job [x] migration path for model configs [x] docs entry and Console toggle [x] perf dashboards updated. Risks and mitigations: speculative prefetch increases KV pressure; mitigated via soft-evict TTL and an adaptive governor that decays aggressive hints when eviction rate rises above threshold. Notes: this PR focuses on orchestration and safety; a follow-up will add model-specific learned horizon estimators using offline traces.

review_comments: Jonah Kim: Can you explain the heuristics used to compute the speculative horizon? I worry about regressions on highly variable streams.

Aisha Patel: The heuristic is conservative by default: we use sequence-length histograms plus an entropy proxy from token logits; aggressive mode is only enabled when prober confidence > 0.8. Added tests that simulate adversarial streams.
Marcel Ortega: We need a clearer metric in the Console for KV thrash so customers can decide to opt out.
Aisha Patel: Added eviction metrics (prefetch_eviction_rate) and Dashboard links in the RFC and Console toggle description.
Priya Shen (approver): Verified 95th percentile improvements and test coverage. Left small nits about naming in prober_service.rs.
Aisha Patel: Addressed nits, renamed sample_horizon -> compute_hint_horizon and expanded comments.
